_note: Verified legal claims permitted in generated FAQ answers. Hand-maintained. Every entry names the evidence that verified it. bin/verify-faq-drafts.php rejects any drafted answer citing an authority absent from this file, and any answer pairing a citation with a quantity this file does not allow.
_why: FAQ answers publish twice - visibly via roden_faq_section() and as FAQPage JSON-LD via roden_schema_faq_page() - so a wrong deadline here is served to AI engines as structured data. Three separate incidents (workers' comp pages carrying the tort SOL, S.C. Code 15-38-15 cited for the plaintiff's bar, 15-78-50 cited for a Tort Claims Act deadline) were all this class of error. Recall is not a source; this file is.

GA 9-3-33.subject: personal injury statute of limitations
GA 9-3-33.claim: Two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury lawsuit in Georgia.
GA 9-3-33.evidence: 226 instances across the existing FAQ corpus; canonical. Restricted from workers' comp contexts because that substitution is the documented 2026-07-30 / 07-31 incident.

SC 15-3-530.subject: personal injury statute of limitations
SC 15-3-530.claim: Three years from the date of injury to file a personal injury lawsuit in South Carolina.
SC 15-3-530.evidence: 241 instances across the existing FAQ corpus; canonical. Same workers' comp restriction.

GA 34-9-82.subject: workers' compensation limitation
GA 34-9-82.claim: One year from the date of the accident to file a workers' compensation claim in Georgia.
GA 34-9-82.evidence: 21 instances in the FAQ corpus; listed in bin/verify-statute-consistency.php $TARGETS.

GA 34-9-80.subject: workers' compensation notice to employer
GA 34-9-80.claim: Notice of a workplace injury must be given to the employer within 30 days.
GA 34-9-80.evidence: Site-consistent across workers' comp practice-area pages. VERIFY BEFORE FIRST USE in a new answer.

SC 42-15-40.subject: workers' compensation limitation
SC 42-15-40.claim: Two years from the date of the accident to file a workers' compensation claim in South Carolina.
SC 42-15-40.evidence: 23 instances in the FAQ corpus, single consistent phrasing; listed in $TARGETS.

SC 42-15-20.subject: workers' compensation notice to employer
SC 42-15-20.claim: Notice of a workplace injury must be given to the employer within 90 days.

GA 51-12-33.subject: comparative fault and apportionment
GA 51-12-33.claim: Georgia bars recovery at 50% or more fault; award reduced by the plaintiff's share below that.
GA 51-12-33.evidence: 116 instances; canonical for Georgia. Note the GA bar is 50%, the SC bar is 51% - do not swap.

Nelson v. Concrete Supply Co..cite: Nelson v. Concrete Supply Co., 303 S.C. 243, 399 S.E.2d 783 (1991)
Nelson v. Concrete Supply Co..subject: comparative negligence bar (plaintiff)
Nelson v. Concrete Supply Co..claim: South Carolina bars a plaintiff who is more than 50% at fault; recovery allowed at 50% or less, reduced by the plaintiff's share.
Nelson v. Concrete Supply Co..evidence: bin/fix-nelson-comparative-bar.php. THIS, NOT S.C. Code 15-38-15, is the authority for the plaintiff's bar. 31 instances across 23 pages miscited 15-38-15 as recently as commit 6c0ee36.

SC 15-38-15.subject: apportionment and joint-and-several liability among DEFENDANTS
SC 15-38-15.claim: Governs allocation of fault among defendants and joint-and-several liability. Does NOT establish the plaintiff's comparative-negligence bar.
SC 15-38-15.evidence: bin/fix-nelson-comparative-bar.php. Correct only for defendant-side apportionment. Use Nelson for the plaintiff's bar.

SC 15-78-110.subject: South Carolina Tort Claims Act limitation
SC 15-78-110.claim: An action against a governmental entity is barred unless commenced within two years of the date the loss was or should have been discovered.

SC 15-78-80.subject: South Carolina Tort Claims Act verified claim (OPTIONAL)
SC 15-78-80.claim: Filing a verified claim with the entity within one year is OPTIONAL and extends the deadline to three years. There is no mandatory pre-suit notice under the SCTCA.
SC 15-78-80.evidence: bin/fix-sctca-mandatory-notice.php. Describing this as a requirement tells a reader with a live claim they have already lost it.

GA 9-3-71.subject: medical malpractice statute of limitations
GA 9-3-71.claim: Two years from the date of injury or discovery, with a five-year statute of repose.

SC 15-3-545.subject: medical malpractice statute of limitations
SC 15-3-545.claim: Three years from the date of injury or discovery, with a six-year statute of repose.

GA 36-33-5.subject: municipal ante litem notice
GA 36-33-5.claim: Ante litem notice against a Georgia municipality must be presented within six months of the injury.
GA 36-33-5.evidence: Listed in $TARGETS; confirmed correct across 11 pages during the 2026-08-31 consistency run.

GA 40-8-76.1.subject: seat belt non-use / seat belt defense
GA 40-8-76.1.claim: Following SB 68 (approved 2025-04-21), subsection (d) permits seat belt non-use to be admitted on negligence, comparative negligence, causation, assumption of risk and apportionment, and it may diminish recovery. There is NO percentage cap on that reduction.
GA 40-8-76.1.evidence: bin/en-fix-seatbelt-defense-sb68.php and bin/en-fix-seatbelt-faqs.php. Three pages previously asserted a 5% cap or a limit that does not exist anywhere in the Act.

SC 56-5-6540.subject: seat belt non-use / seat belt defense
SC 56-5-6540.claim: Subsection (C) provides that a violation is not negligence per se or contributory negligence, and is NOT admissible as evidence in a civil action. Not 'limited' - inadmissible. There is no percentage.
SC 56-5-6540.evidence: bin/en-fix-seatbelt-faqs.php. Three FAQ answers previously described SC as merely 'limiting' admissibility, which is wrong end to end.

GA 40-6-270.subject: duty to stop and render aid after a collision
GA 40-6-270.claim: A driver involved in an accident must stop at the scene or as close as possible, give their name, address and vehicle registration number, show their driver's license, and render reasonable assistance to anyone injured.
GA 40-6-270.evidence: Stated in /blog/georgia-law-on-steps-after-car-accident/ post_content, which sets out the provision's requirements directly.
